rationale.faithfulness: The pre-registered collapse P1 failed again (regime-only wins, no common positive slope on x_att) and the dilution exponent P4 failed; only the unfitted mapping P3 and P5 hold. The natural-experiment tests split (NE43 held, NE42 and the #51 dilution test failed).
rationale.usefulness: Corrects a misleading round-1 lesson (opposite channels) into a concrete one: trim day edges before reading any equal-time gain. The post-hoc k_llm curve now spans all six methods, a candidate knob worth pre-registering, though it fails within #51.

one_line: Loop gains do not collapse onto x_att; the round-1 channel split was day edges; trimmed gains rise with messages per LLM step (post hoc).

v2.adjudication_note: Different claim and provenance: the coordinator scored a composite that included the post hoc day-edge reinterpretation (base 0.20) and called it fragile because the round-1 channel-opposition reading was withdrawn; the blind rater scored the pre-registered collapse failure, which held in every data version. Ruling: score the negative P1 claim at primary base, scoped to R^2 >= 0.5 where the synthetic power is 0.87; credit the synthetic and the data-version robustness once each; fragile is false because the scored headline never changed. The day-edge correction is credited in S, not in p.
